name: Should I hire a framing-only contractor or a full-scope remodeling contractor for a room addition?

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a framing-only contractor or a full-scope remodeling contractor for a room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: While a separate framing crew builds the structural skeleton, choosing a full-service general contractor provides single-source accountability through drywall, painting, and trim. If a standalone framer leaves studs out of plumb or frames rough openings inaccurately, the drywallers and finish carpenters must fix those flaws later, causing extra cost and delays. A hands-on general contractor oversees the framing crew with the final interior finishes in mind, ensuring drywall, tile, and molding install smoothly once framing wraps up.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full-scope contractor oversees framing with finish carpentry, drywall, and sub-trades in mind, preventing structural discrepancies that cause costly finishing delays later.
